ECE 6390

Block codes and Hamming distance

From the figure to the concept

Fig. 1 shows how modulo-two encoding creates legal codewords and distance determines a correction guarantee.

A binary block code maps k information bits to n coded bits, with r = k/n. For a row-vector convention, c = dG mod 2, where d is 1×k, G is k×n and c is 1×n. A column convention uses the transpose. Matrix dimensions and the multiplication order belong together.

The lecture’s teaching example has G rows 100101, 010011 and 001111. Its identity block makes it systematic: the first three output bits reproduce the data. For d = 101, XOR the first and third rows to obtain c = 101010. The model enumerates all eight valid codewords and compares the selected received word using Hamming distance.

The minimum distance between distinct valid words is dmin = 3. Membership checking can detect up to dmin−1 changes, while unique nearest-word decoding can correct up to floor((dmin−1)/2) arbitrary changes. Those are different guarantees. A received word with too many errors can be closer to the wrong valid word.

Nearest Hamming decoding corresponds to equally likely codewords and independent symmetric bit flips with crossover probability below ½. A soft decoder uses the reliability of observations as well. The selected error mask is a reproducible example, not a statistical channel or a guaranteed-recovery claim beyond one arbitrary flipped bit.

Example

For transmitted 101010 and received 101011, the unique nearest valid codeword is 101010 at distance 1. This code corrects that example and every other single-bit error; some two-bit errors are miscorrected. Repeating two copies of a bit only detects disagreement, while three copies support a majority decision.

Practice

1. What is the shape of G when a row of three information bits produces six coded bits?

Make(1×3)G produce 1×6.

G has shape 3×6. A 6×3 matrix belongs to the corresponding column-vector convention with multiplication Gd.

2. Does dmin =3 guarantee that every two-bit error can be corrected?

Compare the detection bound with the correction bound.

It guarantees detection of up to two changed bits when checking valid-word membership, and correction of one arbitrary changed bit. Two-bit nearest-word recovery is not guaranteed.
